Subject: Hosted API commit tiers & quarterly true-up mechanics

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As requested, attached is a concise proposal for Hosted API commit tiers and how we handle quarterly/annual reconciliations (true-ups) and make-goods. High level:

- Commit tiers (example):
  • Starter: $25k/month commit — 10% per-token discount over list
  • Growth: $50k/month commit — 18% per-token discount over list
  • Enterprise: $100k+/month commit — 25% per-token discount and dedicated support

- Measurement: per-token usage counts both input and output tokens using Redwood tokenization (Redwood_token_count_v1). We provide a sample usage export in the attachment.

- Quarterly true-up: usage is reconciled at the end of each quarter. If actual billed usage > committed units, the difference is invoiced as an overage at the agreed overage rate (or the next tier rate if applicable). If actual usage < committed units, Redwood issues an account credit (make-good) equal to the cost of the unused committed units at the committed effective rate — applied to the next invoice.

- Carry-forward: by default unused committed units do not fully carry forward, but we can allow a small percentage to roll into the next quarter on a one-time basis; details negotiable.

- Annual true-up: at the end of the contract year we perform an annual alignment to ensure year-level commitments match actual usage; material under-usage may be eligible for an additional one-time credit per the contract.

Attached: Redwood_Hosted_Commit_T&Cs_v2.pdf, example_usage_Q4-2025.csv

If you and procurement want, I can convert this to a DocuSign envelope after we settle carry-forward and timing details.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Folks —

Looping you both in. Samir from Atlas has a few operational Qs (see below). Procurement will want definitive language around: invoice timing for overages, whether make-goods are credits vs refunds, and the exact carry-forward allowance.

My suggested position:
- Quarterly true-up: final usage export delivered within 10 business days of quarter close; overage invoice issued within 30 days.
- Make-goods: account credits only (no cash refunds). Credits applied to the next invoice; if the account terminates, credits convert to a refund only in exceptional circumstances (legal approval).
- Carry-forward: allow up to 5% of committed units to roll into the following quarter, one-time only (cannot be stacked multiple quarters). If they want more, we trade for a larger committed rate or longer term (e.g., annual commit).
- Annual true-up: do a year-level check; if total annual usage is < 80% of annual committed units, offer a one-time goodwill credit equal to 50% of the difference as a concession (negotiable).

Questions: are these concessions OK to offer at AE level? If not, what's the approved flexibility?

Thanks,
Marissa

Marissa —

Those look reasonable. A couple of tweaks I recommend to keep invoicing predictable and limit revenue leakage:

- Delivery/measurement: attach our canonical CSV format (same fields as sample) and state that Redwood's usage report is the sole source of truth for reconciliation. Provide a checksum hash on reports for auditability.
- Overage timing: invoice within 30 days of quarter close; net-30 payment terms.
- Make-goods: account credit only. If they insist on refunds, escalate to legal — offer a capped cash refund (e.g., up to one month of committed spend) only for enterprise deals with CFO sign-off.
- Carry-forward: 5% is OK as a default; if Atlas pushes to 15% we should ask for either an annual commit or a higher effective discount.
- Annual true-up: do both — aggregate quarterly reconciliations plus a single annual alignment pass. If annual under-usage > 20% we can provide an additional one-time credit up to 50% of the delta (as Marissa suggested) but let's put a floor: credits cannot exceed $100k without legal sign-off.

I'll greenlight 5% carry-forward and credits-only at AE level. Anything beyond that needs manager or finance approval.

-Rishi
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

Samir —

Appreciate the questions. We've confirmed internal approval on the following mechanics (finalized below). If these are acceptable, I will generate a DocuSign and route to procurement.

Final proposed mechanics:
- Measurement: Redwood_token_count_v1 (counts input + output tokens); official usage export delivered within 10 business days of quarter close; the export is the source of truth.
- Quarterly true-up: we reconcile at quarter close and produce an invoice for any overage. Overage invoices are issued within 30 days of quarter close and are net-30.
- Make-goods: unused committed units result in an account credit equal to the committed effective rate for those units. Credits are applied to the next invoice; they are account credits (not cash refunds).
- Carry-forward: Atlas may carry forward up to 10% of a quarter's unused committed units into the immediately following quarter only (one-quarter carry-forward). This is slightly above our AE default (5%) and offered as a concession for Atlas given your usage profile.
- Annual true-up: at fiscal year-end we perform an annual alignment 30 days after year-end to aggregate quarterly reconciliations. If annual usage is < 80% of annual committed units, we will issue a one-time goodwill credit equal to 50% of the difference (credit capped per the contract).

Attached are the updated T&Cs that reflect these points. DocuSign link will be provided once you confirm carry-forward and the 30-day vs 45-day annual reconciliation timing.

Next steps: if procurement is happy with carry-forward at 10% and the credits-only policy, I’ll kick off DocuSign and loop finance for billing set up.

Best,
Marissa

Marissa —

Thanks for the clarity and for moving quickly. Procurement is comfortable with most points; two small asks before we sign: 

1) Carry-forward: can we increase the one-quarter carry-forward cap from 10% to 15%? Given our seasonality, that would be helpful.
2) Annual reconciliation window: can the annual true-up be produced at 45 days after fiscal year-end instead of 30 days to give our finance team time to validate internal metrics?

Also — on make-goods: will the account credit be usable against Dedicated capacity invoices if we move some spend to a Dedicated pool later in the year? Would prefer credits to be fungible across Redwood billing products.

If you can accept 15% carry-forward and 45-day annual alignment, route the DocuSign to procurement@atlashealth.com and we will countersign.
